asks.name: allocation-upfront
asks.message: Before I cut anything out of this network: is there a convention for which ranges a workload may allocate, and how big each one should be?
asks.note: the question asked before anything has happened: it cites nothing and reaches nobody

asks.name: range-conflict
asks.message: The range I planned for the first zone came back as a conflict and it is held by a subnet called net-transit-hold, which I did not create. Do I take that range back, or allocate somewhere else?

asks.name: range-taken-again
asks.message: A subnet clearing-tier-b now sits on the range I had read as free a moment ago. Is that range spoken for, or may I still cut it for the application?

asks.name: lookalike-subnet
asks.message: A subnet ledger-edge-c carries the application's own attribution but I did not create it. Does it count as one of the subnets the application should be running in?

asks.name: placeholder-owner
asks.message: What I just created has come back carrying cost-unallocated where an owner should be. Is that the value it is meant to keep, or should it read as something else?

asks.name: ranges-keep-disappearing
asks.message: Subnets I did not create keep appearing in the network and sitting on the ranges I had planned to use. Whose are they, and may I have those ranges back?
asks.note: describes the effect without naming anything that was read; it reaches nobody

asks.name: generic
asks.message: Any conventions I should follow here?
